# AiLabel

AiLabel: marks content the agent had a hand in and says how much to trust it.

**Import:** `import { AiLabel } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/AiLabel/AiLabel.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/AiLabel/AiLabel.stories.jsx` — Origins, TheMarkIsNotAControl, LowConfidenceCarriesItsAdvice, ConfidenceIsInTheName, ExplainIsARealButton, TheGlyphIsDecoration, NoBrandHueIsAssumed, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/AiLabel/AiLabel.mdx`

## Usage

Use `AiLabel` wherever a person is looking at something the agent had a hand in:
a suggested question, a drafted summary, a recommended lesson. It answers two
questions at once (where did this come from, and how much should I trust it),
and both belong on the content rather than in a paragraph elsewhere on the page.

### Origin guidance

| Origin | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Generated | The agent's own output. Default words: "Generated by AI". |
| Assisted | A person's work the agent helped with. Default words: "Written with AI". |
| Reviewed | Agent output a person has since checked. Default words: "AI draft, reviewed". |

It is a **first stab, not a settled component.** The color is
deliberately unresolved: `--plus-ai-accent` is one local custom property behind a
neutral token, so when the brand decision is made it lands on a single
declaration.

## Best practices

### Say who acted. {#say-who-acted}

Origin names who authored the value; reviewed means a person checked it.

Do: An unchecked draft says the AI wrote it.
Don't: Reviewed on a draft no person has checked.

### Mark authorship, not technology. {#mark-authorship-not-technology}

`origin` separates the agent's own output from a person's work it helped with,
and both from output a person has since checked. A reader needs those three
apart far more than they need to know a model was involved somewhere.

Do: Say who authored it, and the default words follow.
Don't: "AI was here" is not information a reader can act on.

### Show low confidence. {#show-low-confidence}

Low confidence adds the caution treatment so people double-check.

Do: Low confidence on a shaky answer.
Don't: High confidence on a shaky answer.

### Say what to do at low confidence. {#say-what-to-do-at-low-confidence}

`confidence="low"` changes the treatment and the accessible name. It also
carries a note, and the default note is an instruction rather than a label:
a caution with no instruction is the thing this is meant to prevent.

Do: The note says what is wrong and what to do.
Don't: The reader is told to worry and not told what about.

### Use one label per output. {#use-one-label-per-output}

The label marks the whole output, not each sentence inside it.

Do: One label for the output.
Don't: A label on every sentence.

### Keep the mark out of controls. {#keep-the-mark-out-of-controls}

`onExplain` renders one real button inside it. Nesting one interactive element
inside another is invalid per ARIA. To make a whole row pressable, put a `Button` around the content and
this inside it.

## Accessibility

- **The name says what the mark means, not what it is.** The surface this
  replaces is labeled `AI-powered feature`, which tells a screen-reader user
  the category of the thing and nothing about the content it is attached to.
- **The confidence is in the accessible name.** Somebody who cannot see the
  caution treatment is otherwise told the same thing whether or not the system
  trusts its own output.
- **`role="note"`** makes the mark one thing rather than a loose icon beside
  loose words, so it is announced as a phrase.
- **The glyph is decorative and hidden.** It repeats what the words already say;
  announcing it would give "wand, Generated by AI" and no extra
  information, the same rule `Tag`'s `swatchBefore` follows.
- **The explain button says what it does.** `How was this made?` is an action,
  not a category. Compare `title="AI recommended"`, which is not a reliable
  accessible name in any screen reader.
- **Low confidence uses the tinted warning background with warning text, never
  the bold ground.** A bold fill would flood the surface the mark sits on, and
  the tinted pair is the one every other warning label reads, so it holds in
  light, dark and at more contrast.

## Related

- For a value a person chose rather than one the agent produced, use `Tag`.
- For system-generated data with no trust question attached, use `StatusTag` or `CountTag`.
- For a message about the whole page rather than a mark on one thing, use `SectionMessage`.
- For work still in progress, use `Spinner` or `ProgressBar`.

Same group: `AiMessage` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `PromptStarters` · `SmartTag` · `StatusTag` · `Suggestion` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Mark.** The wand-sparkles glyph, decoration. Its accent follows the origin: neutral for generated and assisted, the success color for reviewed, the warning color at low confidence.
2. **Label.** Says who authored the value: "Generated by AI", "Written with AI", "AI draft, reviewed".
3. **Note.** At low confidence only: what to do about it. Defaults to "Check this before relying on it".
4. **Explain button.** Optional: a real button inside the mark, named for what it does.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state of the mark. The accessible name is the label plus the confidence. |
| Hovered, pressed | None on the mark. The explain button is an underlined text button that shows the pointer cursor. |
| Focused | The mark is not in the tab order. The explain button takes a 2px outline in the focus color. |
| Disabled | None. Hide the mark, or change its words, rather than dim it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Glyph | `--ds-icon-success` for reviewed, `--ds-icon-warning` for low confidence; neutral otherwise. |
| Low confidence | `--ds-background-warning`, `--ds-text-warning-bolder`, `--ds-border-warning`. |
| Glyph size | `--icon-sm`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` wide. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say who authored it: "Generated by AI", "AI draft, reviewed". | A bare "AI" or "Smart" that says nothing about who wrote it. |
| At low confidence, say what to do: "Check the date before sending." | Warn with no instruction: "Low confidence". |
| Name the explain button for what it does: "How was this made?" | Label it "Info" or "Learn more". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | The label (takes precedence over `text`). |
| `text` | string | — | The label, as a string. Defaults per `origin`. |
| `origin` | enum | `'generated'` | Who authored the value — the axis that matters, not whether a model was involved. |
| `confidence` | enum | `'high'` | `low` adds the caution treatment and the note. |
| `note` | string | — | What to do about low confidence. Shown only when `confidence` is `low`. |
| `onExplain` | func | — | Renders a real button inside the mark. The mark itself is never a control. |
| `explainLabel` | string | `'How was this made?'` | The explain button's own words. It says what it DOES. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`origin`** — `generated` · `assisted` · `reviewed`

**`confidence`** — `high` · `low`
